newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish motorway winner sees project costing $2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Polish motorway winner sees project costing $2 bln.

text.p: The consortium awarded the concession to build Poland's 364-km A-2 motorway in the west of the country said on Thursday that construction work on the project should cost about $2 billion dollars.

"The financing of our undertaking will gross $2 billion," Autostrada Wielkopolska SA supervisory board chairman Jan Kulczyk told a news conference, adding that about 75 percent of the work would be done by Polish companies.
Consortium deputy president Romuald Zadrozny told Reuters financial costs could bring costs as high as $3 billion.
Autostrada Wielkopolska's main shareholders are Polish Kulczyk Holding with 31.4 percent and Elektrim with 28.4 percent. WBK, Autostrady SA and Warta each have 9.7 percent.
The Autostrady SA consortium includes Budimex, Bank Handlowy SA and Kredyt Bank, among others.
Zadrozny said about 20 percent of the capital for the project would come from the consortium's own funds and 80 percent largely from loans, though bonds were also possible.

He said Autostrada Wielkopolska had signed letters of intent with international organisations such as the EBRD, the Luxembourg-based European Investment Bank, Nordic Investment Bank, Frankfurt-based KFW and the IFC to provide financing.
He said commercial banks ready to finance the project included Deutsche Bank, Commerzbank, Berliner Bank, Societe Generale, Credit Lyonnais and Industrial Bank of Japan.

Zadrozny said WBK should also provide financing and that letters of intent with BRE and BPH to provide credit had also been signed. He said the consortium might need 12 to 18 years to pay off its debts.
Zadrozny also said toll rates were seen at four U.S. cents per kilometre with at least 12,000 cars seen passing daily at the motorway's start.
Kulczyk said an optimistic estimate showed a financial agreement set in this year's third quarter and building starting in the fourth quarter.
Autostrada Wielkopolska president Andrzej Lewandowicz said the motorway would take eight to 10 years to build with the first stretch seen ready in two to three years.

The A-2 motorway would link the central city of Lodz with the German border. Kulczyk said Autostrada Wielkopolska would also seek to enter a tender to be announced perhaps later in 1997 to extend that highway about 100 km toward Warsaw.
Kulczyk said the consortium, along with Bank Handlowy and Budimex, sought to buy shares in builder Dromex, which if bought would take part in construction work.

The consortium has said Strabag International GmbH, Strabag Oestterreich AG, NCC International AB, Impregilo SpA and France's transroute could take part in the construction and operating of the motorway.
